findings_or_changes: 1. Browse the live web and give source URLs? YES. Tested just now: a live search returned current results including a page updated 2026-10-16, with verbatim source URLs. I cite results with source links and check result timestamps, because search-index results can be stale.

2. Read uploaded files (md, json, csv, pdf)? YES, with documented size limits. Tested just now by reading the full PROMPT.md. Uploaded files land in my workspace; PDFs are converted to markdown and paged; large text is paged. Web upload caps (documented): pasted images ~8MB, non-image files ~25MB, videos ~100MB. Zip archives can be unpacked for inspection.

3. Produce files you can download (md, json, csv)? YES. I write files to my workspace and deliver them as chat attachments/Library items with download; temporary public download links are possible but each one needs your one-time approval. This handoff JSON itself is delivered this way.

4. Remember things across separate chats? PARTIAL. Durable facts I choose to save (MEMORY.md) persist and are searchable across all chats, including this side chat. But: each side chat has its own isolated transcript, I do not carry verbatim conversation across chats automatically, and memory search can lag behind the latest file writes. Reliable for curated notes; not photographic. Verified via memory search in this session.

5. Run code? YES. Tested just now: python3 executed (6*7=42), git 2.43.0 present. I have a Linux VM with a shell and can run scripts and install packages. LIMIT: my VM is not your Mac — I cannot run or test anything in your local repo.

6. Access GitHub or other connected tools? PARTIAL. A GitHub connector doc exists but its connection status is NOT_TESTED — I have not verified it is connected. Public GitHub pages are readable via web text fetch; git CLI exists locally. Other connectors are documented as available (Gmail, Google Calendar, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, Spotify, Canva, Stripe, etc.) but each must be status-checked before I rely on it for a task.

7. Which model and context window? I am running on Muse Spark (Muse Spark 1.3), Meta's Muse model family. Context window: 350,000 tokens, reported by the runtime just now (session_status); automatic compaction triggers around 272k tokens. Source: runtime measurement, not a doc quote.

8. Show tokens/usage consumed by a task? PARTIAL. I can show the live context-fill % of the current conversation. I cannot report exact token counts consumed by a past task; usage is tracked against the subscription allowance, not as an exact token balance.

9. Usage limits to plan around? MEASURED just now via the subscription-status check: no paid subscription (free plan); the free weekly allowance is 100% used; it resets Oct 22, 2026 at 3:42 AM EDT. Additional token balance: 4% used, ~1.9B tokens remaining. Exact per-message caps are not published (NOT_TESTED). Practical consequence: heavy Phase 1 research with me now draws on the additional-token balance, so timeboxing Phase 1 matters twice as much.
